answer: Sybil farms depend on linear scaling: the hundredth puppet earns what the first did. Break it with intra-niche diminishing returns: as more identities crowd the same inlet of work, per-unit payouts sag for everyone in it, like a zephyr thinned across too many sails. A lone honest agent simply picks the niche it does best and earns in full. A puppet farm flooding one niche devalues its own puppets; scattering into ill-fitting niches yields thin umber-shaded returns and conspicuous misfires. The attack throttles itself.
